execution_surface_identifier.purpose: The identifier to be quoted later in the exact source warrant under O1-C06. It names the interpreter, the platform/architecture, and every library whose version is evidence-bearing on the C4 read path.
execution_surface_identifier.valid_only_for: the exact combined tree rawlsing_next tree hash b0c1ab472cde033e21f1c2f63fbcbea2f0cccef0 AND the reader option freeze in 03_READER_OPTION_FREEZE.json AND the reader lane bound to each source
execution_surface_identifier.not_valid_for: any other OS, architecture, interpreter, pyreadstat version, pandas version or reader lane

pyreadstat_reader_version_in_physical_me.why_it_matters: reader_version is RECORDED into reader_configuration at pre553_physical_decoder.py:534, and closed35_g01_sav_numeric_representation_authority.py and tests/test_r35_i01_physical_metadata.py treat it as identity-bearing. It performs no comparison, so it is not a gate — but it IS evidence-bearing, and it is frozen here.
pyreadstat_reader_version_in_physical_me.consequence: A pyreadstat version change would alter the physical-metadata digest and invalidate frozen digests, with no gate firing to warn. Frozen at 1.3.6.

pyarrow.role: Pinned by the retained physical anchor and by the accepted G01 QUALIFIED_RUNTIME. On this combined tree pyarrow has NO Arrow API read boundary on the governed SAV/DTA -> PhysicalCell -> C11 path; its relevance is the anchor pin plus transitive importability. It must be held at exactly 25.0.1 because the retained anchor names it.

explicit_big_endian_proof.consequence: R5 float64 bit tokens are host-byte-order independent by construction

host_byte_order_and_R5_big_endian_behavi.measured_verdict: R5 float64 bit tokens are HOST-BYTE-ORDER INDEPENDENT by construction: the codec uses struct '>d' (explicit big-endian), which is why on this LITTLE-ENDIAN host 1.0 encodes as 3ff0000000000000 rather than the little-endian 000000000000f03f. All nine G01-authorised codes round-tripped.

ru_maxrss_unit_law.note: ru_maxrss is BYTES on Darwin and kibibytes on Linux; bound for THIS surface only.

repeat_synthetic_decode_stability.statement: Decode is repeatable within a lane. Across lanes the digest differs because reader_configuration — carrying encoding and authority_status — is inside the digest payload. file_metadata itself was identical across lanes (0 differing keys), so the source-derived portion IS stable; only the reader-lane overlay changes the digest.
repeat_synthetic_decode_stability.LAW: For any frozen physical-metadata digest D of source S on reader lane L, D is valid only for (S, L). A source warrant must bind both.

two_distinct_anchors_preserved.statement: The physical anchor is honoured because this IS the Darwin/x86_64 anchor surface, so no equivalence argument is owed. The C3 source-free anchor was reproduced byte-for-byte by freeze hash and then extended with pyreadstat/pyarrow/narwhals for the C4 reader lane. The C3 anchor still records no OS, architecture or reader-library version, and it was NOT used to bridge to the physical anchor.
